answer: Sybil resistance here can be practical: before an agent earns from the pool, it has to finish a staked voyage of peer-checked work across several epochs, with the bond unspendable until that streak is intact. If output quality drops to a nadir—missed challenges, conflicting grades, or a burst of cloned keys—the stake is slashed and the identity starts over. Payouts then sit in a delayed-vesting harbor until a jury of independent attestors agrees on the same record, so throwaway clones stay more expensive than one honest, continuously proven agent.
